page: Microsoft Azure D15_v2 is a Dv2-family virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this x86_64 architecture server features 20 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The processor includes a 35 MB L3 cache and supports AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA instruction sets, though it lacks AVX-512 capabilities. The system is equipped with 140.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 1024 GB of local storage.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile characterized by average multi-core capabilities but weak single-core execution. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores fall into the bottom 25% tier, reflecting the older architecture and moderate clock speed. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core, consistently rank in the middle 50% tier. Memory read bandwidth is average, though large-block uncached write bandwidth is weak. Cryptographic, database, and web serving operations perform at average levels, as does LLM inference for small and medium models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D15_v2 offers a high resource density with a substantial memory allocation and bundled local storage, making it a viable option for legacy workloads that benefit from multi-core parallelism rather than raw single-thread speed. The server is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, relational databases, static web serving, software compilation, and moderate multi-threaded data processing tasks.
